assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock turned narrow optical transitions in many neutral atoms into a clock with both high stability and very low systematic uncertainty. The magic-wavelength idea removes the lattice Stark shift, so Doppler and recoil effects are suppressed while thousands of atoms are interrogated at once. It resets what can be measured and how accurately, which makes it a very clean measurement-science discovery.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and led the first demonstrations. Ye's group drove the strontium clock to the extreme precision and accuracy regime and developed the laser-coherence and frequency-comb links. The two-name credit is a natural, fair configuration. Others, such as Pierre Lemonde and Hidetoshi's early collaborators, are not in the supplied credit and I cannot assess them from this list.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by many laboratories and in several species. Clocks are at the 10^-18 level and are used for relativistic geodesy and fundamental-physics tests. Recognition is timely and the field has stabilized.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier clock and frequency-comb recognition (2005 prize) may be raised, though the discovery is distinct.
Credit for the lattice-clock concept versus the performance demonstrations is partly intertwined; I am recalling this from general knowledge and have not verified details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Matter-wave atom interferometry turned the wave nature of atoms into a measurement tool with sensitivity to rotation, gravity and gradients, and to fundamental constants such as the fine-structure constant and G. It is a prime example of precision metrology built on laser manipulation of atoms.
assessment.attribution: Pritchard's group made early atom interferometers with nanofabricated gratings and Bordé proposed the Ramsey-Bordé interferometer with laser light. Kasevich built the light-pulse gravimeters, gyroscopes and gradiometers. Chu's role and that of the Chu-Kasevich 1991 work is not in the supplied credit and sits uneasily with the 1997 prize. I would propose all three supplied names but the allocation is unsettled.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed. Gravimeters, gyroscopes and large-baseline experiments are operating, and applications are emerging. Technology is mature enough but some fundamental-physics applications are still developing.
uncertainties: The relationship to the 1997 Nobel Prize for laser cooling may make some members cautious.
Allocation between Bordé, Pritchard and Kasevich is uncertain, and whether Chu's contribution is adequately recognized.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction and subsequent experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators opened a major new class of quantum matter with protected edge and surface states. It is original, conceptually clear and has had a large impact across condensed matter physics.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical proposal in graphene and the Z2 classification, and Molenkamp's group observed the quantum spin Hall effect in HgTe quantum wells after the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang are not in the supplied credit, which leaves a contested configuration. The three supplied names form a plausible prize but are not the whole story.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many experiments, including ARPES on three-dimensional topological insulators. The field is mature, with recognition arguably timely given the 2016 topological-phase prize had a different focus.
uncertainties: Missing credit for the HgTe proposal and for three-dimensional topological insulators (Moore, Balents, Fu, Hasan) is a real fairness concern.
Potential overlap with the 2016 prize on topological phase transitions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Squeezed light allows interferometric measurement below the standard quantum limit. Gravitational-wave detectors now operate with squeezing injected as a routine part of their sensitivity. It is a direct link from quantum optics to practical measurement.
assessment.attribution: Caves supplied the key theoretical proposal for squeezed-state interferometry. Kimble's group and others, including the Slusher group at Bell Labs, produced squeezed states experimentally, and Schnabel's group developed the practical audio-band squeezing used in GEO600 and LIGO. The credited names are a plausible configuration but experimental squeezing credit, such as that of Slusher and Walls, is missing from the supplied list.
assessment.maturity: Implemented in GEO600 and in LIGO and Virgo, so confirmation is strong and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: The role of the LIGO prize (2017) and whether squeezing is seen as a refinement of it.
Experimental priority among early squeezing demonstrations is unresolved by the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cold atoms in optical lattices realize Hubbard-type models with tunable parameters, including the superfluid to Mott insulator transition, and enable quantum simulation of strongly correlated matter, including single-site-resolved quantum gas microscopes. This is original and broad in influence.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch) provided the theory proposing Bose-Hubbard physics in lattices, Greiner (with Hänsch and Bloch) observed the Mott transition, and Bloch led much of the subsequent development. Others, such as Jaksch, Hänsch and Kasevich, are not in the credit, and the configuration leaves the Mott experiment partly unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by many groups worldwide. The field remains active, and quantum simulation of strongly correlated materials is still developing, which leaves some of the headline goals open.
uncertainties: Overlap with the BEC prize of 2001 and with Rydberg-array simulation (B041).
Credit for the original Mott-insulator experiment versus later quantum gas microscopes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED brought strong light-matter coupling into superconducting circuits, creating a platform for quantum information processing and quantum optics in solid state. It is a central architecture for superconducting qubits.
assessment.attribution: Blais and colleagues made the theoretical proposal, Wallraff and Schoelkopf demonstrated strong coupling in 2004 and developed the architecture. The three-name configuration is credible and reasonably clean.
assessment.maturity: Widely confirmed and used by essentially all superconducting-qubit groups. The 2025 prize recognized macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits, and circuit QED is a closely related but distinct step.
uncertainties: Closeness to the 2025 prize may reduce appetite for further superconducting-circuit recognition.
Role of Devoret and Yale colleagues in the architecture beyond the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ti:sapphire lasers, Kerr-lens mode locking and semiconductor saturable absorber mirrors made femtosecond lasers robust and widely available, enabling frequency combs, attosecond science and a broad range of spectroscopy. It is an enabling invention with large impact, though broad instrumentation recognition can feel less fundamental.
assessment.attribution: Moulton invented the Ti:sapphire laser medium, Sibbett's group demonstrated Kerr-lens mode locking, and Keller developed passive mode locking via SESAMs. A fair three-way split exists, but I cannot independently verify the details of the Kerr-lens priority.
assessment.maturity: Mature for decades with extensive commercial and scientific use. Recognition is arguably late rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as an instrument invention of sufficient physical discovery.
Priority questions in Kerr-lens mode locking among several groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal and its experimental realization with trapped ions started controlled quantum logic and quantum computing with individual atoms, leading to quantum simulation and high-fidelity gates. Impact is large and clear.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the 1995 proposal, and Blatt's group performed key experiments, while Wineland's group and NIST demonstrated the first gates. Wineland already shared the 2012 prize, so the experimental allocation is complicated. Zoller also appears in other candidates, which may constrain a combined slate.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation; trapped-ion systems are among the leading quantum computing platforms. Part of the field was already recognized in 2012.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize and with the theory-only candidate B054.
Whether the committee wants to recognize quantum computing hardware at this stage.
